text:
nora: Heads-up — started seeing kernel-swap events on p3-cluster-7 around 09:12 PST and a correlated spike in token tail latency for /v1/chat/stream :chart_with_upwards_trend:
ajay: Ugh. Is this the old selector flip we saw last month or a new behavior?
maya: quick snippet from the logs: 
```
KernelSwap: route=/v1/chat/stream model=redwood-13b quant=4bit prev_kernel=fast_attn_v2 new_kernel=slow_attn_fallback reason=MIG_SLICE_THERMAL
LatencyTail: p50=42ms p95=210ms p99=980ms tokens=avg:3.2
KVCacheEvict: heap=73% evicted=28% policy=auto-prefetch
```
ajay: That reason string is interesting — "MIG_SLICE_THERMAL". We've not encoded that as a selector weight before. Could be thermal throttling causing a kernel fallback to the slower attn path.
elliott: I see simultaneous drop in SM occupancy but VRAM stays high. Maybe slices are being remapped between pods. Dashboard snapshot: sm_occupancy{gpu="g7"}=18% -> 6% at the same time, vram_used stable ~80%.
maya: We also observed a batcher heuristic flip: batcher.swap_threshold changed from 0.65 -> 0.8 in the rollout. That increases tendency to split batches (smaller batches may trigger different kernel path).
nora: TL;DR looks like interplay: thermal -> MIG slice shuffle -> kernel selector sees different slice topology -> picks fallback kernel -> batcher heuristic + smaller batch sizes -> KV cache churn -> token tail spike.
ajay: Can we reproduce on staging? Maybe simulate a MIG slice move and force a kernel-selection recompute.
elliott: I pushed a quick perf probe to staging that toggles MIG visibility. infra-bot: deploy started: rollout/telemetry-probe v0.3 -> staging on p3-staging-2 by elliott
maya: Repro steps I used locally:
```
# simulate low SM occupancy + slice remap
stress-ng --gpu 1 --timeout 30s
# bump batcher param
curl -XPOST http://staging-config/batcher -d '{"swap_threshold":0.8}'
# send 1000 short requests
for i in {1..1000}; do echo '{"input":"hi"}' | http POST http://staging/v1/chat/stream & done
```
ajay: Nice. On staging I saw the kernel-selector metric jump: kernel_choice_count{kernel="slow_attn_fallback"} +1200 during the window. Also KV cache hit ratio dipped: kv_cache_hit=0.67 -> 0.41.
maya: Two actionable things: 1) add a metric to map kernel choice -> MIG slice id / GPU id (token-level tag), 2) add a small cooldown on selector changes when thermal events are detected so we don't cascade to batcher.
nora: Agreed. Also add a token-level latency breakdown per-route that attributes time to: kernel_exec, kv_lookup, batch_wait, network. Right now our token tracer only emits total token time.
elliott: I sketched a Grafana panel query to get per-route token KPIs by kernel: 
```
sum by (route,kernel) (rate(token_latency_bucket[1m]))
sum by (route,kernel) (rate(token_exec_time_sum[1m])) / sum by (route,kernel) (rate(token_count[1m]))
```
maya: For immediate mitigation: revert the batcher.swap_threshold rollout on the affected shard and pin kernel selector to avoid auto-fallback for the next 2h.
ajay: I'll open an ops runbook PR with the steps and add a monitoring alert when kernel_choice_ratio(slow_attn_fallback) > 0.2 for 5m on prod.
nora: Thanks. Action items -- ajay: runbook + alert; elliott: add kernel->gpu mapping metric; maya: rollback batcher param on shard A; infra-bot: mark incident with tag "kernel-swap-thermal"
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-2141001123 by elliott — linked to runbook (private)
maya: quick note for postmortem — include a small timeline with: thermal sensor spike -> MIG remap -> kernel chooser recompute -> batcher heuristic change -> KV churn -> token tail. Helps prevent blame-game. :thumbsup:
nora: I'll start the PM for the postmortem. If anyone captures pprof or flamegraph output, paste here. Especially want to see kernel_exec vs kv_lookup proportions at p95.
ajay: Attaching a tiny flame sample from staging run (copied top lines):
```
flamegraph top:
- kernel_exec 62%
- kv_lookup 18%
- batch_wait 12%
- other 8%
```
maya: Good info. We'll aim to have a dashboard tile tomorrow morning that surfaces kernel_choice_ratio by route + token tail quantiles.
elliott: Also adding an experiment to disable kernel fallback for 1% of traffic to validate baseline.
nora: Cool. Thanks y'all.
